description: The cluster one titled ‘Impact of Marketing Strategies on Brand Preference and Consumer Behaviour’ consists of 70 articles. This cluster identifies varied themes influencing choice and consumer brand preference. Major focus includes the role of market uncertainty in brand selection and promotion strategies, the long-term price effects and the changing dynamics between private labels and national brands (Erdem & Keane, 1996). It also addresses the impact of advertising, new product attributes, and price signals on brand perception and loyalty (Mela et  al., 1997). As a group, these themes present a broad perspective of the strategic and psychological influences behind brand preference in modern consumer markets.

The cluster two titled ‘The Role of Brand Equity, Consumer Perceptions, and Strategic Branding in Shaping Purchase Behaviour’ includes 67 articles. This cluster concentrates on brand equity, consumer preference, and strategic brand positioning in various markets (Cobb-Walgren et  al., 1995). Some of the major themes include self-image congruence, perceived brand authenticity, and corporate social responsibility in influencing purchase intentions (Jamal & Goode, 2001). They also discuss the local-international brand dynamics, store brand behaviour, and efficient brand-building techniques in competitive settings (Schuiling & Kapferer, 2004).

The cluster three titled ‘Exploring the Psychological and Behavioural Influences on Brand Choice: Mediators, Memory, and Contextual Factors’ has 59 articles. This captures the themes of mediation (attitude toward the ad), memory (implicit memory, subliminal priming), emotional and motivational impacts (affective conditioning, time pressure), and contextual factors (ethnocentrism, brand placements) (Karremans et  al., 2006; Pieters & Warlop, 1999; Shimp, 1981).

The cluster four titled ‘The Interplay of Global and Local Brand Perceptions: Cultural, Identity, and Consumer Preferences in Branding Strategies’ consists of 37 articles and emphasise consumer perceptions of global vs. local brand origins, focusing on how national stereotypes, country-of-origin effects, and consumer identity affect brand preferences (Özsomer, 2012; Yadav et  al., 2025; Zhou et  al., 2010). Key factors include price sensitivity, home country bias, and the roles of trust, and cultural alignment (Xie et  al., 2015). The studies also explore the moderating role of foreign brand cues and celebrity endorsements, offering strategic implications for global branding across different markets.

The cluster five ‘Cultural, Psychological, and Contextual Drivers of Brand Preference: Insights into Consumer Behaviour Across Markets’ has 10 articles which underscore how cultural values, psychological needs, and contextual aspects influence consumer orientations, particularly for foreign brands (Hamerman & Johar, 2013; Shepherd et  al., 2015). The driving factors are materialism, religiosity, power distance, and compensatory control, in addition to brand and product symbolism. The study emphasises culturally and psychologically rooted branding approaches sensitive to different markets such as Vietnam, Malaysia, and expatriate communities (Son et  al., 2013).
